To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the radiation sensitivity of enzymes is much higher than that of cells; (2) the radiation sensitivity is dependent upon the enzyme and upon the substrate, and the sensitivity may be altered by the addition of certain substances, such as metals; and (3) the radiation effects are not necessarily due to the direct action of radiation on the enzyme, but may be due to the action on some other substance, e.g. the substrate.

the radiation-induced inactivation of enzymes can be explained by the formation of free radicals in the enzyme molecule, and that the inactivation of enzymes is due to the reaction of the free radicals with the enzyme molecule.
enzymes are not only sensitive to ionizing radiations but also to other physical factors such as temperature, pH, etc.
